Both offices weighed in on all five questions this week, so nothing's excluded from anything below -- the first time that's been true since Week Daze.

# How decisive were these results?

Four of this week's five questions offered three or four choices instead of the usual either-or, so those get the chi-square goodness-of-fit test against "everyone's equally likely" instead of a 50/50 binomial test (see the [Week Daze](../20260909_weekdaze/index.html) post for why). Only "Décor Preference" was a simple two-way question -- more on that one below.


::: {.cell}

:::


**TL;DR:** Best Spice produced the most lopsided result of the week -- Cinnamon alone took 56% of the vote, miles past what you'd expect from 4 equally likely options. Peak Fall Flavor was the closest thing to a real debate: Pumpkin led with just 38%, barely clearing the 1-in-3 chance level and the only question that isn't clearly distinguishable from a random pick.

## Décor Preference


::: {.cell}

:::

# Does HQ agree with RTP?

With three or four options on most questions, "does HQ agree with RTP" mostly means a chi-square test of independence on the full office-by-option table, the same as every multi-option poll since Week Daze. Décor Preference, the lone two-option question, still gets the simpler leader-vs-leader comparison.


::: {.cell}

:::



::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}

1 question flipped the top pick between offices this week: for Favorite Leaf Color, HQ went with Red while RTP leaned Gold -- fittingly, it's also the one question whose office-by-option split clears p < 0.05 (see the table above). That brings the running flip tally to **12**. The other four questions saw both offices land on the same pick.

The Alignment Index for this poll alone comes out to **0.76**, and the cumulative index sits at **0.89**. One real disagreement out of five questions, with reasonably matched enthusiasm everywhere else, is a fairly typical week by this poll's standards.

# Do the basic fall people stick together?

"Cinnamon" swept Best Spice and "Cozy" swept Décor Preference -- about as stereotypically autumnal a pair of landslides as this poll has ever produced, and they drew almost identically sized crowds. Let's bound the overlap.


::: {.cell}

:::


Of the 104 overlapping voters, the cinnamon-loving, cozy-decorating crowd could be as small as 30 or as large as 58 people (29%–56%), versus about 43 (41%) expected if the two preferences were unrelated. Both landslides are large enough that the floor sits comfortably above zero -- there's a real "basic fall" contingent here, not just two big majorities colliding by chance.
